title: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Anthropology - Forensic Anthropology - Biological Profiling - Age
subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: Which of the following biological processes is observed at the end of long bones and is primarily used by anthropologists to estimate the age of a subadult (child or teenager)?
questions.explain: Epiphyseal fusion refers to the closing of growth plates (epiphyses) at the ends of long bones. Because these plates fuse at predictable ages in childhood and adolescence, they are highly reliable for age estimation in subadults.
questions.subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: The squamosal, sagittal, and coronal structures found on the cranium represent immovable joints that close gradually with age. These are referred to as:
questions.explain: Cranial sutures are zigzag-like immovable joints between the bones of the skull. The sequence and degree to which they close (obliterate) provide an estimate for the age of an adult.
questions.subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: Which set of teeth are typically the final permanent teeth to erupt in the human mandible and maxilla, providing evidence that an individual is likely at least 17 to 21 years old?
questions.explain: Third molars (wisdom teeth) typically erupt between 17 and 21 years of age, making them a crucial dental marker for identifying late adolescence or early adulthood.
questions.subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: According to typical fusion sequences, which of the following bones or areas is generally one of the *last* to completely undergo epiphyseal fusion, commonly sealing around the age of 25?
questions.explain: The medial end (sternal end) of the clavicle is renowned for being one of the final growth plates to fuse, generally completing its union between ages 21 and 25.
questions.subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: The sagittal suture connects the two parietal bones along the top of the skull. While variations occur, the complete fusion and near disappearance (obliteration) of the sagittal suture generally suggests the individual was over the age of:
questions.explain: While cranial suture closure is highly variable, the sagittal suture usually completely fuses by the time an individual is in their late 30s to early 40s (often 35+). Therefore, an open sagittal suture suggests a younger adult, and an obliterated one suggests older age.
